20. The fire was observed to have started on the flat roof outside Flats 104 and 105 at about 1451 hours and it engulfed the entire east re-entrant at 1458 hours after about 7 minutes.

21. According to Mr. LI Ka-ching (as provided in Appendix A-24 of [FSD(4)/G(III)/3.24] the Interim Report), a construction worker in Wang Cheong House, he became aware of the fire at about 1450 hours and successfully evacuated to the ground level of Wang Cheong House at about 1500 hours.

22. During his escape from R/F by means of the staircase, he encountered smoke and heat. By the time he reached 14/F, he paused at the lift lobby to catch his breath and recover for about 30 seconds. However, upon returning to the staircase of 14/F, he found it to be filled with dense smoke, making descent impossible. With no other alternatives, he rushed into the lift lobby of 14/F and evacuated successfully by lift.

23. This observation aligns with our hypothesis that the vigorous fire spread along the re-entrant and the resulting smoke and heat would have caused conditions in the staircases to deteriorate rapidly, rendering them untenable for safe evacuation.

24. As shown in Photos 5(a) to (e), the movable boards of the rear staircase between 5/F and 6/F, the front staircase between 10/F and 11/F, and the front staircase between 20/F and 21/F were heavily damaged by fire. Correlating this damage with experimental observations shown in Photo 3(b) suggests that these movable boards might have ignited, with flaming subsequently blocking both escape staircases. Even if those movable boards had not yet been burnt, smoke and heat could still have penetrated into the staircase through the openings of the movable boards at the rear staircase between 15/F and 16/F, as well as between 25/F and 26/F.
